note: Assumptions-and-gaps register for the D2 I-95 pedestrian bridge. Each entry is a small engineering gap, placeholder, assumption or judgment that lives in one place here instead of in decision prose, notebook pending lists, journal text or tracker rows. Hand-edited and committed; the design atlas (design_atlas/build.py) shows the entries on their related nodes and tools/project_coherence.py validates them. An entry records the magnitude the judgment rests on, not the engineering values the journal owns. 'basis' maps register source ids to the SHA-256 the entry was judged against; the generator marks an entry stale when the source register now adopts a different revision of any basis source. Nothing here is generated: the atlas 'Draft assumption' form only produces JSON to paste into 'entries'. Entry shape: {id: A-###, kind: assumption|gap|placeholder|judgment, statement, where, nodes: [atlas node ids], magnitude: {value, unit, sized_by}, disposition: {status: accepted-negligible|pending|closed, decision: D-0xx, on: YYYY-MM-DD}, owner, coherence_items: [COH-###], basis: {source id: sha256}, references: [repository paths]}.

entries.statement: The pier FBMP export (Pier_Fixed.XML, D-077, 22 October 2026) models the pier wall as extra members hung between pile nodes: four vertical 36 x 60 in concrete members (library section 5, 150 pcf), one per pile, from pile point 2 (EL 40.20, 18.9 in below the cap axis) to pile point 11 at the soil surface (EL 26.05), 169.8 in long, 31.83 kip each (127.3 kip in all), plus 30 weightless 36 x 20.52 in ties (section 4, 1 pcf) between adjacent piles at ten levels; direct wind is applied at the mid-height wall nodes 49, 83 and 117. The 21 October export (D-073) had the members running to pile point 13 (EL 19.72, 184.4 kip), 6 ft below the soil surface, because they had followed earlier soil elevation changes; the user reran the model to correct them. Against the CAD wall (219 x 36 x 194.86 in, EL 24.53 to 40.76, 133.4 kip): the model wall is 240 in long, 6.1 kip lighter (4.6%), its top 6.8 in below the cap bottom and its bottom 18.3 in above the CAD wall bottom. Traced down each pile the axial drops below the head (the wall members take the load) and returns at point 11 with the wall weight; the pier pile structural checks govern there (Pu 252.0 kip, Strength III, pile 4, element 11), while the Factored Design Load of the Pile Data Table is the pile-head compression (226.1 kip, Strength I), which excludes the wall weight that enters below the head (the pile-head sums balance only the applied loads plus the cap self-weight). Re-judged 22 October 2026 against the D-078 ring wall case (ring plate 1/2 in; wall, forces and free length unchanged) and the T037 journal. Re-judged the same day against the D-079 CAD model (ring plates 1/2 in; the CAD wall concrete, 133.4 kip, is unchanged, and the ring steel, 276 lb in place of 414 lb, is in neither weight, so the 6.1 kip gap stands). Re-judged 22 October 2026 against the T039 journal (C018 Pier Cap Cheek Wall Design added after C017 under D-081; every other module byte-identical to the T037 revision). Re-judged 22 October 2026 against the T040 journal (C006 Pier Wall, Hairpins and Fin Plates withdrawn under D-082; C017 regenerated with identical values; every other module byte-identical to the T039 revision). Re-judged 22 October 2026 against the D-083 CAD model (pier wall SDM bar marks 5G1/5G2/5G3 written on the 124 wall bars; naming only, no geometry, quantity or exposed face changed, so the judgment stands). Re-judged 22 October 2026 against the D-084 ring wall case (LRFD 10th edition development, 27-in U legs; the wall, forces and free length unchanged), the D-085 CAD model (U legs 27 in, marks 5G1-5G3) and the T041 journal. Re-judged 23 October 2026 against the T042 journal (C001-C004, C015 and C016 list each input under its own section, D-087; only the position of input definitions changed, every formula and value is that of the T041 revision).
